label: copy phase: re-input g (from orig pos >=2) when next output is t or g
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely (96% of mass) on steps whose input is the fed-back token g; the remaining 4% are fed-back t steps whose next output is also t (t t repeats). It never fires when g is copied from original position 0 or 1 (recall_idx <= 2 is rare and weak), nor in the original or delimiter phases. Magnitude depends strongly on the token being output next: g followed by t (a g t bigram in the original) gives the largest activations (top examples ~0.75-1.0 of max, 64% of mass, and 90% precision when recall_idx >= 3); g followed by g is moderate; g followed by other tokens (e, 2, y, ...) gives weak, sparse activations. Copy-phase g in general is a poor predictor (precision ~5%) because most g re-inputs that are not followed by t/g stay silent. The chosen predicate captures ~71% of mass on dev with precision ~0.64; the long tail of weak g->other activations is missed.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=g (+7.00), in_tok=g (+4.64), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+4.04), phase=2 & out_tok=t (+3.97), out_tok=t (+3.77), next_out=t (+3.59). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.08), recall_idx=1 (-3.35), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.35), phase=2 & out_tok=a (-2.75).
